daas-irab:1-7.t:
﴿اسْمَ﴾: Regarding its derivation, the people of Basra held that it is derived from السمو, which is elevation, while the people of Kufa held that it is derived from السمة, which is a mark (sign). The alif was dropped in the basmala because of its frequent use. ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾: its pattern is فعلان and it carries the meaning of intensiveness (mubālagha); none is described by it except Allah the Exalted.
﴿الرَّحِيمِ﴾: its pattern is فعيل and it likewise carries the meaning of intensiveness.
﴿بِسْمِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "ابتدئ" (I begin), or to an omitted khabar (predicate), its implied form being "ابتدائي" (my beginning). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of Allah. ﴿الرَّحِيمِ﴾: a second naʿt.
The clause of the basmala is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), a clause with no grammatical position. «[Note: Please refer to the introduction to learn the method of the book.]» ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾: praise of something beautiful by speech. ﴿الرب﴾: the Owner and the Master; it may also mean the One who sets right and the Nurturer. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾: plural of عالَم (with fatḥa on the lām), and it means all created beings. ﴿يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾: the Day of Recompense. ﴿الصِّراطَ﴾: the path. It is treated as masculine and feminine, the masculine being more common.
﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and both are attached to an omitted khabar, its implied form being "الحمد واجب" (praise is due).
﴿رَبِّ﴾: a naʿt of Allah, or a badal (substitute) from it. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural.
﴿الرَّحْمنِ، الرَّحِيمِ﴾: two naʿts of Allah. ﴿مالِكِ﴾: a third naʿt. ﴿يَوْمِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الدِّينِ﴾: a second muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿إِيَّاكَ﴾: a detached accusative pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿نَعْبُدُ﴾: an imperfect verb. ﴿وَإِيَّاكَ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿نَسْتَعِينُ﴾: an imperfect verb; its original form is نستعون — they found the kasra on the wāw heavy and transferred it to the ʿayn, and the wāw turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. ﴿اهْدِنَا﴾: an imperative verb intended as supplication, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter.
The fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you), and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الصِّراطَ﴾: a noun, accusative by removal of the preposition — or a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾: a naʿt of الصراط; its original form is مستقوم, like نستعين. ﴿صِراطَ﴾: a badal from الصراط — a badal of the whole from the whole. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿أَنْعَمْتَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the fāʿil; the clause أنعمت is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to أنعمت. ﴿غَيْرِ﴾: a naʿt of الذين. ﴿الْمَغْضُوبِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: both attached to المغضوب. ﴿وَلَا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is redundant (zāʾida), to reinforce the meaning of negation in غير. ﴿الضَّالِّينَ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to المغضوب عليهم, genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿آمين﴾: a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr) for supplication — it is not part of al-Fātiḥa — meaning "استجب" (answer [our prayer]); indeclinable on sukūn, and it was vowelled with fatḥa to suit the yāʾ preceded by a kasra.
